layercake_v25.architecture: LayerCake route-isolated shallow sparse core host

v1_artifact_facts.english_external_contract: strict UTF-8 bytes to strict UTF-8 bytes
v1_artifact_facts.english_execution_schema: LayerCake width-768 three-block decoder plus package-owned GPT-2 tokenizer, router, five sparse residual routes, guards, and incremental state
v1_artifact_facts.specialist_external_contract: strict UTF-8 bytes to strict UTF-8 bytes
v1_artifact_facts.specialist_execution_schema: package-private width-64 encoder-decoder pointer machine with a package-private lexeme vocabulary

mismatches.evidence: English tensor namespaces model.*, router.*, and residual.* are instantiated by the LayerCake v25 ShallowSparseEnglishCore and router/residual implementations; neither transformer model class declares this ABI.
mismatches.resolution: Define a host-neutral capability virtual machine and runtime class registry. Do not load these tensors into Qwen or Pythia blocks.

mismatches.evidence: English width is 768, Qwen width is 896, Pythia width is 768, and specialist width is 64. Equal Pythia width does not imply equal coordinates.
mismatches.resolution: Private widths remain private. The canonical boundary uses typed fields and byte anchors rather than direct hidden-state tensors.

mismatches.evidence: English carries GPT-2 vocabulary 50,257; Qwen declares 151,936 entries; Pythia declares 50,304; each specialist package carries a distinct lexeme table.
mismatches.resolution: Decode host input to strict UTF-8, preserve exact byte anchors, and encode canonical output into the frozen host tokenizer with exact round-trip verification.

mismatches.evidence: Qwen uses full RoPE with theta 1,000,000; Pythia uses partial rotary position encoding; the package runtimes own their own sequence positions.
mismatches.resolution: Canonical position is an explicit monotone sequence index and byte-span table. Host-private positional encodings remain outside capability state.

mismatches.evidence: Qwen uses RMSNorm, Pythia uses LayerNorm, and package-owned modules carry their own normalization tensors.
mismatches.resolution: Canonical numeric channels have explicit L2 normalization; private host norms are never exposed to capabilities.

mismatches.evidence: The LayerCake residual routes are trained in its private width-768 basis. Qwen and Pythia hidden coordinates have no identified alignment, including when the width happens to match.
mismatches.resolution: V1 residual tensors remain inside their declared capability runtime. They are not projected into receiver residual streams. A future latent capability format would require newly certified V2 artifacts.

mismatches.evidence: LayerCake v25 and the portable specialist decoders own custom persistent incremental state; Qwen and Pythia expose different cache structures.
mismatches.resolution: Version a host-independent state envelope with capability-owned opaque state and host-owned opaque state in separate namespaces.

mismatches.evidence: English produces GPT-2-token logits, specialists produce lexeme/pointer actions, and receiver heads produce their own vocabulary logits.
mismatches.resolution: Capabilities emit canonical output intent plus authoritative UTF-8 anchors. Host adapters realize anchors through native tokenizers and verify exact byte reconstruction.

mismatches.evidence: V1 route selection and guard state are owned by LayerCake host classes, while transformer caches and attention masks are owned by their model classes.
mismatches.resolution: Declare disjoint generic-runtime, capability, adapter, and host-base ownership; reject any capability-specific host parameter.

mismatches.evidence: V1 artifacts declare fp32; Qwen metadata declares bfloat16 and Pythia metadata declares float16.
mismatches.resolution: Capability mathematical execution remains fp32 under the registered runtime. Host codec equality is exact bytes; other numeric channels use preregistered tolerances.

mismatches.evidence: LayerCake authenticates, parses, adopts storage, registers routes, and releases ownership. Hugging Face causal LM loading has no corresponding capability lifecycle.
mismatches.resolution: One capability-blind certification freezes a lifecycle adapter implementing verify, load, register, activate, deactivate, remove, and reinstall without optimization.

mismatches.evidence: Specialist artifacts declare direct_selected_one_cake_no_router and distinct private tokenizer hashes; they cannot be blended as ordinary transformer residual adapters.
mismatches.resolution: Preserve direct selected execution and package-private tokenization. The generic host adapter registers declarative capability identities but never fits a per-domain projection.

mismatches.evidence: Qwen2ForCausalLM and GPTNeoXForCausalLM accept their own state dictionaries and caches but expose no lc-direct-neural-core/25 or lc-direct-neural-decoder/1 consumer.
mismatches.resolution: Certify a small architecture-specific codec/lifecycle adapter against the canonical runtime before any capability is available.

governing_decision.do_not_attempt: No LayerCake-to-Qwen/Pythia residual projection, per-capability bridge, tokenizer transplant, or receiver-specific capability tuning is authorized.
governing_decision.v2_initial_hypothesis: A capability-blind host codec and lifecycle adapter plus a host-neutral canonical capability runtime can preserve the unchanged byte-bound V1 packages across all three host environments.
governing_decision.provider_bypass_boundary: Calling the LayerCake v25 host from Qwen or Pythia remains forbidden. The V2 implementation must use a host-neutral runtime contract, must exercise each frozen host tokenizer and checkpoint during conformance, and must report that V1 capabilities remain self-contained rather than claiming transplantation into receiver weights.
